facts.fact: GitLab, Automattic, and Doist are known for remote or distributed work practices and extensive documentation, but saying all three have literally written handbooks for everything is an overstatement.
aliases: GitLab Automattic Doist literally written handbooks for everything employees guidance
facts.verification: The underlying point about documented remote-work practices is supported, but the absolute wording 'literally written handbooks for everything' is too broad to verify as stated.

facts.fact: GitLab is an all-remote company that publishes a public remote-work handbook and extensive documentation.
facts.verification: The local KB records GitLab as a well-known all-remote organization with a public handbook/documentation model.

facts.fact: Automattic has a distributed workforce and has publicly documented remote/distributed work practices.
facts.verification: The local KB supports the claim that Automattic operates with a distributed workforce; the stronger phrase 'handbooks for everything' is rhetorical.

facts.fact: Doist is a remote-first company known for asynchronous communication and documentation practices.
facts.verification: The local KB supports Doist as a remote-first company associated with asynchronous work practices.

facts.fact: Hospitals and radiology workflows use AI-assisted systems to help interpret medical images such as X-rays and prioritize urgent cases.
aliases: hospitals use AI reading X-rays flagging urgent cases
facts.verification: The local KB confirms real-world assistive AI use in medical imaging and prioritization; it does not imply clinician replacement.

facts.fact: The US FDA reviews and regulates many AI-enabled medical devices and software functions when they meet medical-device definitions.
aliases: FDA regulatory barriers AI medical devices
facts.verification: The local KB confirms FDA oversight of qualifying AI/ML-enabled medical devices; the statement that 'full autonomy isn't happening anytime soon' is predictive rather than verifiable.

facts.fact: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated adoption of telehealth and digital-health tools, though the exact effect on AI adoption varies by segment.
aliases: pandemic accelerated digital health adoption including AI tools
facts.verification: The local KB supports accelerated digital-health adoption during the pandemic; attributing the entire AI adoption trend to the pandemic would be too broad.

facts.verification: The local KB supports both privacy risk and dataset-bias concerns in healthcare AI, while the severity varies by system and dataset.
